technicalEvidenceLimits: I did not recompute any hash, triangle multiset, UV loop, packed-image hash or GLB channel binding. The geometry and technical facts are accepted as reported, not verified by me.

The JSON files I read do contain these consistent statements: all279MeshNames/Matrices/Parents exact; all278OtherMesh exact; wp82ExactRetainedR4 true; 38,500 triangles; 266 protected and 13 changed appearance owners; 21 graphs preserved, W03FragmentEdge missing, 0 changed; 16 WP82 source faces were the only uses of W03FragmentEdge, with 0 replacement uses.
The fragment-edge scope file states its own limit: it covers visible mesh face use only and makes no claim about non-mesh datablock references.
Only five native isolation probes were run, so not all 279 owners have current visibility probes. My whole-view observations cannot stand in for that coverage.

I identified parts (P29 box, WP23 roof field, WP30 basket) by their position in the views. I did not inspect mesh IDs. The WP23 = turret-roof causal field mapping is inferred from the W03P23CausalClone graph name.
The WP27 focus images are a renderer-only isolation. The frame-filling 128 focus image does not show whole-vehicle game-scale recognition.
findingsVerbatimParsed.geometryTechnicalCorrectness: Accepted as reported: PASS on the stated scope. I saw no new geometry, framing change or bounds change compared with r3 at the same bounds. The ground fragment and overall silhouette are identical in position.
findingsVerbatimParsed.relativeWorkingRetention: Retention looks good across the whole vehicle. Hull, running gear, front glacis, gun, smoke banks and the deck grille look identical to r3. The front-hull condition stays clean, as the brief intends. All changes are confined to the bustle, the turret roof, the box and the fragment.

categoryObjections.wholeForm: No objection. The silhouette and proportions are unchanged, and no catastrophic form was added, which matches the brief.
categoryObjections.referenceFidelity: Partial. In both analogues the char/paint-loss boundaries are hard-edged, lacy and mottled, with paint and ash/bare-metal patches mixed through the dark zone. Current r4 is a single smooth radial gradient with almost no high-frequency breakup and no visible scorched-tan rim with a broken edge. It matches the brief's 'connected field' and 'restrained' requirements, but not the source morphology of coating loss.
categoryObjections.connectionAppearance: The field is now connected across the roof, the bustle sides and the cupola surround, and it reads as one event. That is better than r3. Remaining issues: (a) In the right-view box, a jagged black zig-zag on the bustle side reads as a decal or graphic rather than an opening. (b) In the top view, a long black wedge along the left bustle edge reads as a flat black slab. (c) In the left view, the gradient mostly reads as a soft shadow cast toward the rear.
categoryObjections.finishStyle: Main objection: at 1000 the char still reads as airbrushed soot or ambient-occlusion shading, not fire-driven coating loss. The falloff is uniform and centred, with no edge character, no blistering or flaking boundary, and no lighter heat-bleached or ash zones inside the dark field. The cause is mask frequency and edge character, not palette.
categoryObjections.conditionRecognition: At 1000 and 256 rear-three-quarter and top, a localized burn on the rear turret is recognizable. At 128 it degrades to 'dark patch on the rear turret roof': plausible as damage, but also readable as shadow or dark paint. The front three-quarter at 128 carries it weakly, and the front view not at all (occluded, as declared).
categoryObjections.readability: The roof and bustle field reads at 256 in rear-three-quarter and top. At 128 the cavity and hatch holes merge into the field, and only overall value carries the condition.

predeclaredQuestions.Q1_wholeFinish: Yes: the connected field clearly improves on r3's pale-gray, camouflage-like islands, which I compared directly at 1000 and 256 rear-three-quarter and 1000 top. Yes: at 1000 it still reads airbrushed, as shadow or soot, not fire or coating loss. As a working direction it is the best current one. It is not finished.
predeclaredQuestions.Q2_wp27: I did not see the previous pale radial or mip lines in whole 256/128 or focus 256/128 (rear-three-quarter and top). The limit is finite visual inspection, not a pixel-level guarantee. Cavity depth reads clearly at focus 1000 and 256, with a visible wall/floor value step under shadows, separate from the roof char. At focus 128 it reads as a darker rectangle, separable mainly by value. Not-seen limit: the cavity is a fairly clean chamfered rectangle, with no lip, peel or torn rim. It reads as an engineered pocket more than a blowout opening. That is a geometry or owner matter, not a finishing one. The two round hatch interfaces read as intact, as stated. Minor: faint vertical banding on the left side face in focus 1000 rear-three-quarter.
predeclaredQuestions.Q3_p29: Risk confirmed in the actual views. Front-three-quarter 1000: a large black angular region with a jagged top rim. Right 1000: a jagged black zig-zag that reads as a graphic. Top 1000: a black slab or wedge. I accept that the open box is real geometry, but that is not a visual waiver. The hard mesh-boundary transitions are the cause, so finishing cannot fully resolve this.
predeclaredQuestions.Q4_wp30: I see no diagonal streak on the basket in current rear-three-quarter or top. The diagonal on the deck/grille in the top view matches antenna and cast shadows, and I am not judging it as paint. Basket finish: dark gray rails are controlled and do not compete with the field. They slightly merge with the char at 256, which is acceptable. I make no claim about UV for any streak.
predeclaredQuestions.Q5_wp82: The fragment now reads dark and scorched, not pale gray as in r3. A thin tan exposed-edge sliver is visible at 1000 (front, top, rear-three-quarter). At 256 and 128 it is only a speck. That is adequate for its role. I am not requesting a new shape, and the whole views do not amount to close-up finish approval.
predeclaredQuestions.Q6_contextAndScale: Untouched teal glass and bright cupola/hatch rims sit inside the char field and stand out at 1000 rear-three-quarter and top. I am not overriding the optics protection, but this is a visible inconsistency for finish readiness. Antenna bases are clean. The front is occluded and the sides are weak: left reads as shading, right as the graphic issue. At 128 the condition is marginal but present in rear-three-quarter and top. I do not require all-around damage or a catastrophic silhouette.

perPartObservations.WP27_BustleArmor: Connected char. No radial or mip lines seen at 256/128. Cavity depth reads. The cavity rim is too clean for a blowout (geometry note). Not seen: underside, interior beyond the visible floor, the all-pixel guarantee.
perPartObservations.WP23_roofField_inferred: The roof field is continuous with the bustle and has the smooth airbrushed falloff described above. The hatch outline plate is visible within the field. Not seen: mesh-ID confirmation.
perPartObservations.WP29_openBox: Black slab and jagged graphic read in front-three-quarter, right and top. The hard mesh-boundary transition is the driver. Not seen: an interior close-up, so I make no claims about box windows.
perPartObservations.WP30_basket: Controlled contrast. No streak observed. Shadows left untouched. Not seen: a basket close-up.
perPartObservations.WP82_fragment: Quiet scorch with a short tan edge cue, visible only at 1000. Not seen: close-up.

decisions.rationale: The connected field is the right direction and is better than r3. It is not finish-ready, for two reasons: the airbrushed edge character at 1000, and P29's slab/graphic reading. Neither is a palette problem.

priorityCorrections: 1. P29 hard boundaries: send to the source/owner phase for a decision on the torn-rim geometry and boundary of the box. Do not try to fix it with finishing.

2. Char edge character: within the existing 15 maps and UVs, the coating-loss boundary needs breakup, meaning an irregular hard-edged rim and some lighter heat or ash patches inside the field, following the source morphology. This is mask authoring, not palette.
3. Optional, after 1–2: decide as an owner matter how the protected clean glass and cupola rims will be handled visually inside the field. Do not alter the protection unilaterally.
findingsVerbatimParsed.retentionVsReturn: Keep the current r4 working bytes as the baseline for part-role inspection. After five whole finishes, do not run another palette-only whole retry. Send P29 to the source/owner phase. Do the char edge-character correction only as a targeted mask/breakup change on the retained bytes, after part-role inspection.
